title: On-call & Incident Response Playbook — Comprehensive
author: Jordan Lee
summary: Canonical on-call and incident response playbook for Redwood Inference: process, runbooks for common failure modes, postmortem expectations, on-call rotations and escalation, game day guidance, and status page / customer communication templates.
content:
Overview

Purpose:
- Provide a single, actionable reference for on-call engineers and incident commanders at Redwood Inference.
- Reduce time-to-detection, standardize triage, ensure consistent customer communications, and accelerate reliable recovery.

Scope:
- Applies to all production-hosted, dedicated, and private deployment control planes and inference runtime services managed by Redwood.
- Includes infra (GPU fleet, autoscaling, routing), control plane, API gateway, console, and customer-facing status page communications.

Key principles:
1) Safety of customer workloads and data integrity come first.
2) Triage quickly; mitigate impact before root cause analysis.
3) Communicate early and often to internal and external stakeholders.
4) Capture actions and timeline in the incident ticket; follow with a timely postmortem and actionable remediation.

Roles & Responsibilities

- First Responder (On-call Engineer): initial detection, basic triage, containment, updates to incident channel and ticket.
- Incident Commander (IC): owns coordination, priority decisions, communications, and escalation.
- Subject Matter Experts (SMEs): provide deep-dive investigation and remediation for specific subsystems (runtime, orchestration, networking, billing).
- Communications Lead: drafts status page and customer emails with IC review.
- Engineering Manager / Pager Backup: approves escalations and manages resource allocation.

Severity levels & SLOs

Severity classification (quick reference):
- Sev-1 (P0): Complete outage or data loss impacting >20% of customers or critical revenue paths. Target response: <5 minutes; IC assigned within 10 minutes.
- Sev-2 (P1): Major degradation (latency >2x SLO or throughput degraded) affecting multiple customers. Target response: <15 minutes.
- Sev-3 (P2): Isolated customer impact or minor functionality loss. Target response: <60 minutes.
- Sev-4 (P3): Non-critical operational issues, cosmetic bugs, or scheduled maintenance.

SLOs & error budgets referenced: see /confluence/eng-sre/slo-and-error-budgets (production latency 95th < 1200ms for hosted API; platform availability 99.95% monthly).

Incident lifecycle (step-by-step)

1) Detection & Alerting
- Alerts can originate from monitoring (Prometheus/Alertmanager, Datadog), customer reports, or telemetry (high error-rates, model-serving backpressure).
- On-call engineer must acknowledge the alert in the paging system (PagerDuty) within the target response time for the severity.
- Create or link an incident ticket in the canonical tracker (Jira/INC-XXXXX). Add one-line summary.

2) Triage (First 15 minutes)
- Evidence collection checklist (First Responder):
  - Collect timeline of alerts/errors and affected services.
  - Check high-level dashboards: token throughput, GPU utilization, queue depths, autoscaler events, ingress errors.
  - Verify whether the issue is limited to a region, cluster, or model variant.
  - Determine potential customer impact and estimated blast radius.
- IC assignment: If escalation beyond first responder is required, IC is assigned and a dedicated Slack incident channel is created (channel name: #inc-YYYYMMDD-brief).

3) Mitigation & Containment
- Prioritize mitigating customer impact over root-cause analysis. Typical mitigations:
  - Roll back recent deploys via the deployment runbook.
  - Route traffic to healthy regions or fallback model variants.
  - Scale up Dedicated capacity (burst pools) or temporarily increase autoscaler caps.
  - Blackhole noisy customers or cancel long-running batches.
- Document all actions and timestamps in the incident ticket.

4) Communication
- Internal updates: every 15-30 minutes for Sev-1, every 30-60 minutes for Sev-2 until stable.
- External updates: first customer-facing update within 30 minutes for Sev-1; within 2 hours for Sev-2. Use status page templates below.
- Use the status page and targeted emails for customers with active incidents (see templates).

5) Recovery & Verification
- Verify recovery by confirming metrics return to baseline and new errors are not introduced.
- Run synthetic checks (end-to-end smoke tests) for affected routes/models.
- Mark incident as resolved in PagerDuty and update ticket with final resolution summary.

6) Postmortem & Follow-up
- Postmortem deadline: draft within 72 hours of incident resolution; final postmortem with action items within 10 business days.
- Assign owners for each action item and track in a dedicated Jira epic.
- Prioritize long-term fixes, monitoring improvements, playbook updates, and customer remediation if needed.

Runbooks — common incident types

A) High API latency (hosted inference)
Steps (ordered):
1. Confirm alert: check API gateway error rate, 95th/99th latency, and p95 token generation time.
2. Check runtime fleet: GPU utilization, queue depth, and KV cache hit-rate.
3. If backlog present, temporarily increase downstream consumer concurrency and autoscaler target for inference workers.
4. Route high-latency traffic to a lower-latency region or cached model variant.
5. If recent deploy suspected, rollback to previous revision (deployment runbook link).
6. Communicate via status page and internal channel.

B) GPU capacity exhaustion / OOM on runtime nodes
1. Identify affected node pool and scheduler errors (OOM/killed processes).
2. Increase pool size or scale up instance type (if capacity available).
3. Evacuate and cordon nodes showing repeated OOMs; restart failed runtime containers with clean cache.
4. Temporarily enforce stricter batching limits or reduce max_seq_length to reduce memory pressure.
5. If root cause is model change or regression, pin deployment to the last known-good model and rollback.

C) Control plane auth/permission failures
1. Confirm whether KMS/HSM or identity provider (IdP) incidents are occurring.
2. If KMS outage, use emergency key-access procedure and notify security lead.
3. Fail closed vs fail open decision: default is fail-closed for customer data protection unless approved by security.

D) Failed rollout / Canary regression
1. Detect via canary metrics: high error-rate or latency for canary cohort.
2. Immediately halt rollout and promote rollback via deployment automation.
3. Capture artifacts (canary logs, request traces) and open a rollback incident if needed.

Escalation matrix & contact info

- On-call Engineer -> Senior On-call -> Incident Commander -> Eng Manager -> VP Engineering
- Pager escalation times: 5m -> 10m -> 20m -> 30m for Sev-1.
- Contact list (primary):
  - Eng SRE Lead: Priya Menon (pager: +1-555-0101)
  - Runtime Lead: Miguel Rivera (pager: +1-555-0102)
  - Platform Lead: Sofia Martinez (pager: +1-555-0103)
  - Security on-call: Rahul Desai (pager: +1-555-0104)

On-call rotations and scheduling

- Primary on-call schedule: weekly rotation by team. Engineering teams maintain their own rotation calendars in the on-call schedule tool (Opsgenie/PagerDuty).
- Shift rules:
  - Primary: 7 days (Mon 00:00 to Sun 23:59)
  - Secondary / backup: two-week overlap to allow knowledge transfer for cross-team incidents.
  - Weekend coverage: paid on-call shift and defined follow-on working hours if incident exceeds 2 hours.
- Handoff checklist for shift changes:
  1. Review open incidents and tickets.
  2. Share ongoing mitigations and next steps in the rotation channel.
  3. Confirm escalation contacts and runbook access.

Game days (testing incident readiness)

Purpose:
- Validate runbooks, communications, and cross-team coordination.

Cadence & scope:
- Quarterly company-wide game day focusing on critical flows (model serving, autoscaler, KMS failover).
- Monthly team-level tabletop exercises for new features and recent incidents.

Game day checklist (ops):
- Pre-game: define objectives, success criteria, and rollback backstops.
- During: log timelines, observe adherence to runbooks, and capture communication artifacts.
- Post-game: publish a short report with improvements and update playbooks within 7 days.

Status page & customer communication templates

Status page entry structure (recommended fields):
- Title: short one-line (e.g., "Partial degradation of hosted text generation — us-west")
- Impact: concise summary of affected customers and functionality.
- Timeline: key timestamps and actions taken.
- Current status: investigating / mitigated / resolved.
- Next update: ETA for next update if not resolved.
- Workaround: if applicable.

External customer templates (editable)

1) Initial notification (Sev-1):
Subject: [Redwood] Incident affecting hosted inference — immediate notification
Body:
Hello,

We are aware of a service disruption affecting hosted inference in {region}. Our on-call team is actively investigating. We will post updates to https://status.redwood.ai and provide the next update by {ETA}. We apologize for the impact and appreciate your patience.

If you are experiencing production-impacting issues not covered above, please reply to this email and include your account ID.

Sincerely,
Redwood Inference Operations

2) Status update template:
Subject: [Redwood] Incident update — {short summary}
Body:
Update at {timestamp}: We have identified {root_cause_summary_or_progress}. Mitigation steps taken: {list}. Impacted customers: {estimate}. Next update by {ETA}.

3) Resolved notification:
Subject: [Redwood] Incident resolved — {short summary}
Body:
The incident affecting {services/region} has been resolved as of {timestamp}. Root cause (preliminary): {short summary}. Actions taken: {list of fixes}. Postmortem ETA: {date}.

Postmortem template & expectations

Minimum sections for a public/internal postmortem (separate constructs when customer-sensitive data involved):
- Title, incident id, severity, owner(s), timeline (detailed with timestamps), detection, impact (customers, metrics), root cause analysis (contributing factors), remediation & mitigations (short-term), long-term actions, action owners and due dates, lessons learned, monitoring and alerting changes, references (logs, traces, runbook links).

Timeline expectations:
- Draft postmortem: within 72 hours of resolution (internal).
- Final postmortem: within 10 business days with assigned action owners.
- Customer-facing summary: available within 10 business days for incidents where customers were affected.

Blamelessness and follow-up:
- Postmortems should be blameless and focus on system/process fixes. Individual mistakes are not called out.
- Ensure at least one measurable improvement per Sev-1 incident (monitoring, runbook change, deployment guardrail, or automation).

Playbook maintenance & governance

- Runbook authorship: teams owning a service are responsible for maintaining runbooks and updating them after each relevant incident or game day.
- Quarterly review: on-call and incident response playbook reviewed quarterly by Eng SRE.
- Change process: updates to this playbook require a reviewer from Eng SRE and one additional cross-functional reviewer before publishing.

Appendices

Appendix A — Quick runbook snippets
- Rollback CLI (safe): curl -X POST https://deploy.redwood.ai/api/rollback -d '{"service":"inference-runtime","rev":"<previous>"}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>'
- Evacuate node (kubectl): kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force

Appendix B — Example incident channel naming conventions
- #inc-YYYYMMDD-sev1-brief (primary incident channel)
- #war-room-<service>-<id> (deep-dive channels)

Appendix C — Links and references
- SLOs & error budgets: /confluence/eng-sre/slo-and-error-budgets
- Deployment runbook: /confluence/eng-platform/runbooks/deployment-runbook-2025
- Status page templates: /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/incident-communications-and-status-page-templates-2026

If there are questions about this playbook or to request a game day, contact the Eng SRE lead or open an internal RFC in the eng-sre workspace.
